subject.title: /stop abort leaves streaming card in idle state, blocking subsequent messages (replies=0)

question: Should maintainers require a live Feishu WebSocket/CardKit trace before allowing a repair, or is the current source-level active-abort reproduction enough to start a shared reply-lifecycle fix with Feishu regression coverage?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible but not live-reproduced on current main, and the repo already carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` plus maintainer-review/live-repro labels, so automation should not choose the shared-vs-Feishu repair boundary alone.

options.title: Require live Feishu trace first
options.body: Keep the issue in maintainer review until a redacted Feishu `/stop` then follow-up trace captures session key, reply-operation state, queuedFinal, counts, dispatcher failures, and streaming-card close/idle logs.

options.title: Authorize source-level repair
options.body: Let a maintainer sponsor a focused repair from the current active-abort test and require Feishu dispatcher/card tests before merge.

options.title: Split shared and Feishu work
options.body: Track the shared active-abort zero-reply path separately from Feishu CardKit closeout if live proof shows two distinct failures.

recommendation.title: Require live Feishu trace first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue in maintainer review until a redacted Feishu `/stop` then follow-up trace captures session key, reply-operation state, queuedFinal, counts, dispatcher failures, and streaming-card close/idle logs.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved proof gap is Feishu-specific tenant/CardKit behavior, and the package metadata names this handle as the Feishu/Lark community maintainer signal.
